    34→# Mechanical detectors → subjective dimensions they provide evidence for.
    35→# When findings from these detectors change during a scan, the corresponding
    36→# subjective assessments are marked stale so reviewers know to re-evaluate.
    37→_DETECTOR_SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSIONS: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
    38→    "structural": ("design_coherence", "abstraction_fitness"),
    39→    "smells": ("design_coherence", "error_consistency"),
    40→    "global_mutable_config": ("initialization_coupling",),
    41→    "coupling": ("cross_module_architecture",),
    42→    "layer_violation": ("cross_module_architecture",),
    43→    "private_imports": ("cross_module_architecture",),
    44→    "dupes": ("convention_outlier",),
    45→    "boilerplate_duplication": ("convention_outlier",),
    46→    "naming": ("convention_outlier",),
    47→    "flat_dirs": ("package_organization",),
    48→    "orphaned": ("design_coherence",),
    49→    "uncalled_functions": ("design_coherence",),
    50→    "responsibility_cohesion": ("design_coherence", "abstraction_fitness"),
    51→    "cycles": ("cross_module_architecture", "dependency_health"),
    52→}
    53→
    54→
    55→def _mark_stale_on_mechanical_change(
    56→    state: StateModel,
    57→    *,
    58→    changed_detectors: set[str],
    59→    now: str,
    60→) -> None:
    61→    """Mark subjective assessments stale when mechanical findings change.
    62→
    63→    Only marks dimensions that already have an assessment — doesn't create
    64→    new entries for dimensions that have never been reviewed.
    65→    """
    66→    assessments = state.get("subjective_assessments")
    67→    if not isinstance(assessments, dict) or not assessments:
    68→        return
    69→
    70→    affected_dims: set[str] = set()
    71→    for detector in changed_detectors:
    72→        dims = _DETECTOR_SUBJECTIVE_DIMENSIONS.get(detector, ())
    73→        affected_dims.update(dims)
    74→
    75→    if not affected_dims:
    76→        return
    77→
    78→    for dimension in sorted(affected_dims):
    79→        if dimension not in assessments:
    80→            continue
    81→        payload = assessments[dimension]
    82→        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
    83→            continue
    84→        # Placeholders have never been scored — nothing to mark stale.
    85→        if payload.get("placeholder"):
    86→            continue
    87→        # Don't overwrite if already stale
    88→        if payload.get("needs_review_refresh"):
    89→            continue
    90→        payload["needs_review_refresh"] = True
    91→        payload["refresh_reason"] = "mechanical_findings_changed"
    92→        payload["stale_since"] = now
    93→
    94→
    95→@dataclass
    96→class MergeScanOptions:
    97→    """Configuration bundle for merging a scan into persisted state."""
    98→
    99→    lang: str | None = None
   100→    scan_path: str | None = None
   101→    force_resolve: bool = False
   102→    exclude: tuple[str, ...] = ()
   103→    potentials: dict[str, int] | None = None
   104→    merge_potentials: bool = False
   105→    codebase_metrics: dict[str, Any] | None = None
   106→    include_slow: bool = True
   107→    ignore: list[str] | None = None
   108→    subjective_integrity_target: float | None = None
   109→
   110→
   111→def merge_scan(
   112→    state: StateModel,
   113→    current_findings: list[dict],
   114→    options: MergeScanOptions | None = None,
   115→) -> ScanDiff:
   116→    """Merge a fresh scan into existing state and return a diff summary."""
   117→    ensure_state_defaults(state)
   118→    resolved_options = options or MergeScanOptions()
   119→
   120→    now = utc_now()
   121→    _record_scan_metadata(
   122→        state,
   123→        now,
   124→        lang=resolved_options.lang,
   125→        include_slow=resolved_options.include_slow,
   126→        scan_path=resolved_options.scan_path,
   127→    )
   128→    _merge_scan_inputs(
   129→        state,
   130→        lang=resolved_options.lang,
   131→        potentials=resolved_options.potentials,
   132→        merge_potentials=resolved_options.merge_potentials,
   133→        codebase_metrics=resolved_options.codebase_metrics,
   134→    )
   135→
   136→    existing = state["findings"]
   137→    ignore_patterns = (
   138→        resolved_options.ignore
   139→        if resolved_options.ignore is not None
   140→        else state.get("config", {}).get("ignore", [])
   141→    )
   142→    current_ids, new_count, reopened_count, current_by_detector, ignored_count, upsert_changed = (
   143→        upsert_findings(
   144→            existing,
   145→            current_findings,
   146→            ignore_patterns,
   147→            now,
   148→            lang=resolved_options.lang,
   149→        )
   150→    )
   151→
   152→    raw_findings = len(current_findings)
   153→    suppressed_pct = _compute_suppression(raw_findings, ignored_count)
   154→
   155→    ran_detectors = (
   156→        set(resolved_options.potentials.keys())
   157→        if resolved_options.potentials is not None
   158→        else None
   159→    )
   160→    suspect_detectors = find_suspect_detectors(
   161→        existing,
   162→        current_by_detector,
   163→        resolved_options.force_resolve,
   164→        ran_detectors,
   165→    )
   166→    auto_resolved, skipped_other_lang, skipped_out_of_scope, resolve_changed = auto_resolve_disappeared(
   167→        existing,
   168→        current_ids,
   169→        suspect_detectors,
   170→        now,
   171→        lang=resolved_options.lang,
   172→        scan_path=resolved_options.scan_path,
   173→        exclude=resolved_options.exclude,
   174→    )
   175→
   176→    # Mark subjective assessments stale when mechanical findings changed.
   177→    changed_detectors = upsert_changed | resolve_changed
   178→    if changed_detectors:
   179→        _mark_stale_on_mechanical_change(

1→"""Zone classification system — deterministic file intent classification.
     2→
     3→Classifies files into zones (production, test, config, generated, script, vendor)
     4→based on path patterns. Zone metadata flows through findings, scoring, and the LLM.
     5→"""
     6→
     7→from __future__ import annotations
     8→
     9→import logging
    10→import os
    11→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
    12→from enum import Enum
    13→
    14→from desloppify.base.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
    15→from desloppify.engine.policy.zones_data import (
    16→    CONFIG_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    17→    SCRIPT_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    18→    SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
    19→    TEST_SKIP_DETECTORS,
    20→)
    21→
    22→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    23→
    24→
    25→class Zone(str, Enum):
    26→    """File intent zone — determines scoring and detection policy."""
    27→
    28→    PRODUCTION = "production"
    29→    TEST = "test"
    30→    CONFIG = "config"
    31→    GENERATED = "generated"
    32→    SCRIPT = "script"
    33→    VENDOR = "vendor"
    34→
    35→
    36→# Zones excluded from the health score
    37→EXCLUDED_ZONES = {Zone.TEST, Zone.CONFIG, Zone.GENERATED, Zone.VENDOR}
    38→
    39→# String values for quick lookup in scoring (findings store zone as string)
    40→EXCLUDED_ZONE_VALUES = {z.value for z in EXCLUDED_ZONES}
    41→
    42→
    43→@dataclass
    44→class ZoneRule:
    45→    """A classification rule: zone + list of path patterns.
    46→
    47→    Patterns are matched against relative file paths. First matching rule wins.
    48→    Pattern types (auto-detected from shape):
    49→      - "/dir/"   → substring match on full path (directory marker)
    50→      - ".ext"    → basename ends-with (suffix/extension, e.g. ".d.ts", ".test.")
    51→      - "prefix_" → basename starts-with (trailing underscore)
    52→      - "name.py" → basename exact match (has extension, no /)
    53→      - fallback  → substring on full path
    54→    """
    55→
    56→    zone: Zone
    57→    patterns: list[str]
    58→
    59→
    60→def _match_pattern(rel_path: str, pattern: str) -> bool:
    61→    """Match a zone pattern against a relative file path.
    62→
    63→    See ZoneRule docstring for pattern type conventions.
    64→    """
    65→    basename = os.path.basename(rel_path)
    66→
    67→    # Directory pattern: "/dir/" → substring on padded path
    68→    if pattern.startswith("/") and pattern.endswith("/"):
    69→        return pattern in ("/" + rel_path + "/")
    70→
    71→    # Suffix/extension pattern: starts with "." → contains on basename
    72→    if pattern.startswith("."):
    73→        return pattern in basename
    74→
    75→    # Prefix pattern: ends with "_" → basename starts-with
    76→    if pattern.endswith("_"):
    77→        return basename.startswith(pattern)
    78→
    79→    # Suffix pattern: starts with "_" → basename ends-with (_test.py, _pb2.py)
    80→    if pattern.startswith("_"):
    81→        return basename.endswith(pattern)
    82→
    83→    # Exact basename: has a proper file extension (1-5 chars after last dot),
    84→    # no "/" → exact basename match (config.py, setup.py, conftest.py)
    85→    if "/" not in pattern and "." in pattern:
    86→        ext = pattern.rsplit(".", 1)[-1]
    87→        if ext and len(ext) <= 5 and ext.isalnum():
    88→            return basename == pattern
    89→
    90→    # Fallback: substring on full path (vite.config, tsconfig, eslint, etc.)
    91→    return pattern in rel_path
    92→
    93→
    94→# ── Common zone rules (shared across languages) ──────────
    95→
    96→COMMON_ZONE_RULES = [
    97→    ZoneRule(Zone.VENDOR, ["/vendor/", "/third_party/", "/vendored/"]),
    98→    ZoneRule(Zone.GENERATED, ["/generated/", "/__generated__/"]),
    99→    ZoneRule(Zone.TEST, ["/tests/", "/test/", "/fixtures/"]),
   100→    ZoneRule(Zone.SCRIPT, ["/scripts/", "/bin/"]),
   101→]
   102→
   103→
   104→def classify_file(
   105→    rel_path: str, rules: list[ZoneRule], overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None
   106→) -> Zone:
   107→    """Classify a file by its relative path. Overrides take priority."""
   108→    if overrides:
   109→        override = overrides.get(rel_path)
   110→        if override:
   111→            try:
   112→                return Zone(override)
   113→            except ValueError as exc:
   114→                log_best_effort_failure(
   115→                    logger, f"parse zone override for {rel_path}", exc
   116→                )
   117→    for rule in rules:
   118→        for pattern in rule.patterns:
   119→            if _match_pattern(rel_path, pattern):
   120→                return rule.zone
   121→    return Zone.PRODUCTION
   122→
   123→
   124→class FileZoneMap:
   125→    """Cached zone classification for a set of files.
   126→
   127→    Built once per scan from file list + zone rules.
   128→    """
   129→
   130→    def __init__(
   131→        self,
   132→        files: list[str],
   133→        rules: list[ZoneRule],
   134→        rel_fn=None,
   135→        overrides: dict[str, str] | None = None,
   136→    ):
   137→        """Build zone map.
   138→
   139→        Args:
   140→            files: List of file paths (absolute or relative).
   141→            rules: Ordered zone rules (first match wins).
   142→            rel_fn: Optional function to convert paths to relative.
   143→            overrides: Manual zone overrides {rel_path: zone_value}.
   144→        """
   145→        self._map: dict[str, Zone] = {}
   146→        self._overrides = overrides
   147→        for f in files:
   148→            rp = rel_fn(f) if rel_fn else f
   149→            self._map[f] = classify_file(rp, rules, overrides)
   150→
   151→    def get(self, path: str) -> Zone:
   152→        """Get zone for a file path. Returns PRODUCTION if not classified."""
   153→        return self._map.get(path, Zone.PRODUCTION)
   154→
   155→    def exclude(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   156→        """Return files NOT in the given zones."""
   157→        zone_set = set(zones)
   158→        return [f for f in files if self._map.get(f, Zone.PRODUCTION) not in zone_set]
   159→
   160→    def include_only(self, files: list[str], *zones: Zone) -> list[str]:
   161→        """Return files that ARE in the given zones."""
   162→        zone_set = set(zones)
   163→        return [f for f in files if self._map.get(f, Zone.PRODUCTION) in zone_set]
   164→
   165→    def counts(self) -> dict[str, int]:
   166→        """Return file count per zone."""
   167→        counts: dict[str, int] = {}
   168→        for zone in self._map.values():
   169→            counts[zone.value] = counts.get(zone.value, 0) + 1
   170→        return counts
   171→
   172→    def production_count(self) -> int:
   173→        """Count files classified as production."""
   174→        return len(self._map) - self.non_production_count()
   175→
   176→    def non_production_count(self) -> int:
   177→        """Count files in excluded zones (test/config/generated/vendor)."""
   178→        return sum(1 for z in self._map.values() if z in EXCLUDED_ZONES)
   179→
   180→    def all_files(self) -> list[str]:
   181→        """Return all classified file paths."""
   182→        return list(self._map.keys())
   183→
   184→    def items(self) -> list[tuple[str, Zone]]:
   185→        """Return all (path, zone) pairs."""
   186→        return list(self._map.items())
   187→
   188→
   189→# ── Zone detection policies ────────────────────────────────
   190→
   191→
   192→@dataclass
   193→class ZonePolicy:
   194→    """Per-zone detection policy.
   195→
   196→    skip_detectors: detectors to skip entirely for this zone.
   197→    downgrade_detectors: detectors whose confidence is downgraded to "low".
   198→    exclude_from_score: whether findings in this zone are excluded from scoring.
   199→    """
   200→
   201→    skip_detectors: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
   202→    downgrade_detectors: set[str] = field(default_factory=set)
   203→    exclude_from_score: bool = False
   204→
   205→
   206→ZONE_POLICIES: dict[Zone, ZonePolicy] = {
   207→    Zone.PRODUCTION: ZonePolicy(),
   208→    Zone.TEST: ZonePolicy(
   209→        skip_detectors=TEST_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   210→        downgrade_detectors={"smells", "structural"},
   211→        exclude_from_score=True,
   212→    ),
   213→    Zone.CONFIG: ZonePolicy(
   214→        skip_detectors=CONFIG_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   215→        exclude_from_score=True,
   216→    ),
   217→    Zone.GENERATED: ZonePolicy(
   218→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   219→        exclude_from_score=True,
   220→    ),
   221→    Zone.VENDOR: ZonePolicy(
   222→        skip_detectors=SKIP_ALL_DETECTORS,
   223→        exclude_from_score=True,
   224→    ),
   225→    Zone.SCRIPT: ZonePolicy(
   226→        skip_detectors=SCRIPT_SKIP_DETECTORS,
   227→        downgrade_detectors={"structural"},
   228→    ),
   229→}
   230→
   231→
   232→# ── Helpers for phase runners ─────────────────────────────
   233→
   234→
   235→def adjust_potential(zone_map, total: int) -> int:
   236→    """Subtract non-production files from a potential count.
   237→
   238→    Uses the zone map's own file list — no need to pass files separately.
   239→    No-op if zone_map is None.
   240→    """
   241→    if zone_map is None:
   242→        return total
   243→    return max(total - zone_map.non_production_count(), 0)
   244→
   245→
   246→def should_skip_finding(zone_map, filepath: str, detector: str) -> bool:
   247→    """Check if a finding should be skipped based on zone policy.
   248→
   249→    Returns True if the file's zone policy says to skip this detector.
   250→    """
   251→    if zone_map is None:
   252→        return False
   253→    zone = zone_map.get(filepath)
   254→    policy = ZONE_POLICIES.get(zone)
   255→    return policy is not None and detector in policy.skip_detectors
   256→
   257→
   258→def filter_entries(
   259→    zone_map, entries: list[dict], detector: str, file_key: str = "file"
   260→) -> list[dict]:
   261→    """Filter detector entries by zone policy. No-op if zone_map is None.
   262→
   263→    If file_key points to a list (e.g. cycle entries with "files"), checks
   264→    the first element.
   265→    """
   266→    if zone_map is None:
   267→        return entries
   268→
   269→    def _get_path(entry):
   270→        val = entry[file_key]
   271→        return val[0] if isinstance(val, list) else val
   272→
   273→    return [
   274→        e for e in entries if not should_skip_finding(zone_map, _get_path(e), detector)
   275→    ]
   276→

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from dataclasses import dataclass, field
     6→
     7→from desloppify.engine._scoring.policy.core import (
     8→    CONFIDENCE_WEIGHTS,
     9→    FAILURE_STATUSES_BY_MODE,
    10→    HOLISTIC_MULTIPLIER,
    11→    SCORING_MODES,
    12→    ScoreMode,
    13→    detector_policy,
    14→)
    15→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import Finding
    16→
    17→# Tiered file-count cap thresholds for non-LOC file-based detectors.
    18→# Controls how many findings per file contribute to the weighted failure sum.
    19→_FILE_CAP_HIGH_THRESHOLD = 6     # findings in file for high cap
    20→_FILE_CAP_MID_THRESHOLD = 3      # findings in file for mid cap
    21→_FILE_CAP_HIGH = 2.0             # cap value at high concentration
    22→_FILE_CAP_MID = 1.5              # cap value at mid concentration
    23→_FILE_CAP_LOW = 1.0              # cap value at low concentration (1-2 findings)
    24→
    25→
    26→def merge_potentials(potentials_by_lang: dict[str, dict[str, int]]) -> dict[str, int]:
    27→    """Sum potentials across languages per detector."""
    28→    merged: dict[str, int] = {}
    29→    for lang_potentials in potentials_by_lang.values():
    30→        for detector, count in lang_potentials.items():
    31→            merged[detector] = merged.get(detector, 0) + count
    32→    return merged
    33→
    34→
    35→def _iter_scoring_candidates(
    36→    detector: str,
    37→    findings: dict[str, Finding],
    38→    excluded_zones: frozenset[str],
    39→):
    40→    """Yield in-scope findings for a detector (zone-filtered)."""
    41→    for finding in findings.values():
    42→        if finding.get("suppressed"):
    43→            continue
    44→        if finding.get("detector") != detector:
    45→            continue
    46→        if finding.get("zone", "production") in excluded_zones:
    47→            continue
    48→        yield finding
    49→
    50→
    51→def _finding_weight(finding: Finding, *, use_loc_weight: bool) -> float:
    52→    """Compute the scoring weight for a single finding."""
    53→    if use_loc_weight:
    54→        return finding.get("detail", {}).get("loc_weight", 1.0)
    55→    return CONFIDENCE_WEIGHTS.get(finding.get("confidence", "medium"), 0.7)
    56→
    57→
    58→def _file_count_cap(findings_in_file: int) -> float:
    59→    """Tiered cap for non-LOC file-based detectors.
    60→
    61→    Keeps file-count denominator semantics while preserving concentration signal:
    62→    1-2 findings => _FILE_CAP_LOW, 3-5 => _FILE_CAP_MID, 6+ => _FILE_CAP_HIGH.
    63→    """
    64→    if findings_in_file >= _FILE_CAP_HIGH_THRESHOLD:
    65→        return _FILE_CAP_HIGH
    66→    if findings_in_file >= _FILE_CAP_MID_THRESHOLD:
    67→        return _FILE_CAP_MID
    68→    return _FILE_CAP_LOW
    69→
    70→
    71→@dataclass
    72→class _ModeAccum:
    73→    """Per-mode accumulator for file-based detector scoring."""
    74→
    75→    by_file: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    76→    by_file_count: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict)
    77→    file_cap: dict[str, float] = field(default_factory=dict)
    78→    holistic_sum: float = 0.0
    79→    issue_count: int = 0
    80→
    81→
    82→def _file_based_failures_by_mode(
    83→    detector: str,
    84→    findings: dict[str, Finding],
    85→    policy,
    86→) -> dict[ScoreMode, tuple[int, float]]:
    87→    """Accumulate weighted failures by score mode for file-based detectors."""
    88→    accum: dict[ScoreMode, _ModeAccum] = {mode: _ModeAccum() for mode in SCORING_MODES}
    89→
    90→    for finding in _iter_scoring_candidates(detector, findings, policy.excluded_zones):
    91→        status = finding.get("status", "open")
    92→        holistic = finding.get("file") == "." and finding.get("detail", {}).get(
    93→            "holistic"
    94→        )
    95→
    96→        for mode in SCORING_MODES:
    97→            if status not in FAILURE_STATUSES_BY_MODE[mode]:
    98→                continue
    99→
   100→            if holistic:
   101→                accum[mode].holistic_sum += (
   102→                    _finding_weight(finding, use_loc_weight=False) * HOLISTIC_MULTIPLIER
   103→                )
   104→                accum[mode].issue_count += 1
   105→                continue
   106→
   107→            weight = _finding_weight(finding, use_loc_weight=policy.use_loc_weight)
   108→            file_key = finding.get("file", "")
   109→            a = accum[mode]
   110→            a.by_file[file_key] = a.by_file.get(file_key, 0.0) + weight
   111→            a.by_file_count[file_key] = a.by_file_count.get(file_key, 0) + 1
   112→            if policy.use_loc_weight and file_key not in a.file_cap:
   113→                a.file_cap[file_key] = weight
   114→            a.issue_count += 1
   115→
   116→    out: dict[ScoreMode, tuple[int, float]] = {}
   117→    for mode in SCORING_MODES:
   118→        a = accum[mode]
   119→        if policy.use_loc_weight:
   120→            weighted = sum(
   121→                min(weighted_sum, a.file_cap.get(file_key, weighted_sum))
   122→                for file_key, weighted_sum in a.by_file.items()
   123→            )
   124→        else:
   125→            weighted = sum(
   126→                min(weighted_sum, _file_count_cap(a.by_file_count.get(file_key, 0)))
   127→                for file_key, weighted_sum in a.by_file.items()
   128→            )
   129→        out[mode] = (a.issue_count, weighted + a.holistic_sum)
   130→    return out
   131→
   132→
   133→def detector_stats_by_mode(
   134→    detector: str,
   135→    findings: dict[str, Finding],
   136→    potential: int,
   137→) -> dict[ScoreMode, tuple[float, int, float]]:
   138→    """Compute (pass_rate, issue_count, weighted_failures) for each score mode."""
   139→    if potential <= 0:
   140→        return {mode: (1.0, 0, 0.0) for mode in SCORING_MODES}
   141→
   142→    # Review and concern findings are scored via subjective assessments only —
   143→    # exclude them from the detection-side scoring pipeline so resolving these
   144→    # findings never changes the score directly.
   145→    if detector in ("review", "concerns"):
   146→        return {mode: (1.0, 0, 0.0) for mode in SCORING_MODES}
   147→
   148→    policy = detector_policy(detector)
   149→
   150→    if policy.file_based:
   151→        mode_failures = _file_based_failures_by_mode(detector, findings, policy)
   152→    else:
   153→        issue_count: dict[ScoreMode, int] = {mode: 0 for mode in SCORING_MODES}
   154→        weighted_failures: dict[ScoreMode, float] = {
   155→            mode: 0.0 for mode in SCORING_MODES
   156→        }
   157→
   158→        for finding in _iter_scoring_candidates(
   159→            detector, findings, policy.excluded_zones
   160→        ):
   161→            status = finding.get("status", "open")
   162→            weight = _finding_weight(finding, use_loc_weight=False)
   163→            for mode in SCORING_MODES:
   164→                if status not in FAILURE_STATUSES_BY_MODE[mode]:
   165→                    continue
   166→                issue_count[mode] += 1
   167→                weighted_failures[mode] += weight
   168→
   169→        mode_failures = {
   170→            mode: (issue_count[mode], weighted_failures[mode]) for mode in SCORING_MODES
   171→        }
   172→
   173→    out: dict[ScoreMode, tuple[float, int, float]] = {}
   174→    for mode in SCORING_MODES:
   175→        issues, weighted = mode_failures[mode]
   176→        pass_rate = max(0.0, (potential - weighted) / potential)
   177→        out[mode] = (pass_rate, issues, weighted)
   178→    return out
   179→
   180→
   181→def detector_pass_rate(
   182→    detector: str,
   183→    findings: dict[str, Finding],
   184→    potential: int,
   185→    *,
   186→    strict: bool = False,
   187→) -> tuple[float, int, float]:
   188→    """Pass rate for one detector.
   189→
   190→    Returns (pass_rate, issue_count, weighted_failures).
   191→    Zero potential -> (1.0, 0, 0.0).
   192→    """
   193→    mode: ScoreMode = "strict" if strict else "lenient"
   194→    return detector_stats_by_mode(detector, findings, potential)[mode]
   195→
   196→
   197→__all__ = [
   198→    "detector_pass_rate",
   199→    "detector_stats_by_mode",
   200→    "merge_potentials",
   201→]
   202→

     8→
     9→def find_suspect_detectors(
    10→    existing: dict,
    11→    current_by_detector: dict[str, int],
    12→    force_resolve: bool,
    13→    ran_detectors: set[str] | None = None,
    14→) -> set[str]:
    15→    """Detectors that had open findings but likely did not actually run this scan."""
    16→    if force_resolve:
    17→        return set()
    18→
    19→    previous_open_by_detector: dict[str, int] = {}
    20→    for finding in existing.values():
    21→        if finding["status"] != "open":
    22→            continue
    23→        detector = finding.get("detector", "unknown")
    24→        previous_open_by_detector[detector] = (
    25→            previous_open_by_detector.get(detector, 0) + 1
    26→        )
    27→
    28→    # 'review' findings enter via `desloppify review --import`, not via scan phases.
    29→    # They are always marked suspect so the scan never auto-resolves them.
    30→    import_only_detectors = {"review"}
    31→    suspect: set[str] = set()
    32→
    33→    for detector, previous_count in previous_open_by_detector.items():
    34→        if detector in import_only_detectors:
    35→            suspect.add(detector)
    36→            continue
    37→        if current_by_detector.get(detector, 0) > 0:
    38→            continue
    39→        if ran_detectors is not None:
    40→            if detector not in ran_detectors:
    41→                suspect.add(detector)
    42→            continue
    43→        if previous_count >= 3:
    44→            suspect.add(detector)
    45→
    46→    return suspect
    47→
    48→
    49→def auto_resolve_disappeared(
    50→    existing: dict,
    51→    current_ids: set[str],
    52→    suspect_detectors: set[str],
    53→    now: str,
    54→    *,
    55→    lang: str | None,
    56→    scan_path: str | None,
    57→    exclude: tuple[str, ...] = (),
    58→) -> tuple[int, int, int, set[str]]:
    59→    """Auto-resolve open/wontfix/fixed/false_positive findings absent from scan.
    60→
    61→    Returns (resolved, skipped_other_lang, skipped_out_of_scope, resolved_detectors).
    62→    """
    63→    resolved = skipped_other_lang = skipped_out_of_scope = 0
    64→    resolved_detectors: set[str] = set()
    65→
    66→    for finding_id, previous in existing.items():
    67→        if finding_id in current_ids or previous["status"] not in (
    68→            "open",
    69→            "wontfix",
    70→            "fixed",
    71→            "false_positive",
    72→        ):
    73→            continue
    74→
    75→        if lang and previous.get("lang") and previous["lang"] != lang:
    76→            skipped_other_lang += 1
    77→            continue
    78→
    79→        if scan_path and scan_path != ".":
    80→            prefix = scan_path.rstrip("/") + "/"
    81→            if (
    82→                not previous["file"].startswith(prefix)
    83→                and previous["file"] != scan_path
    84→            ):
    85→                skipped_out_of_scope += 1
    86→                continue
    87→
    88→        if exclude and any(matches_exclusion(previous["file"], ex) for ex in exclude):
    89→            continue
    90→
    91→        if previous.get("detector", "unknown") in suspect_detectors:
    92→            continue
    93→
    94→        previous_status = previous["status"]
    95→        previous["status"] = "auto_resolved"
    96→        previous["resolved_at"] = now
    97→        previous["suppressed"] = False
    98→        previous["suppressed_at"] = None
    99→        previous["suppression_pattern"] = None
   100→        previous["resolution_attestation"] = {
   101→            "kind": "scan_verified",
   102→            "text": "Disappeared from detector output",
   103→            "attested_at": now,
   104→            "scan_verified": True,
   105→        }
   106→        previous["note"] = (
   107→            "Fixed despite wontfix — disappeared from scan (was wontfix)"
   108→            if previous_status == "wontfix"
   109→            else "Disappeared from scan — likely fixed"
   110→        )
   111→        resolved_detectors.add(previous.get("detector", "unknown"))
   112→        resolved += 1
   113→
   114→    return resolved, skipped_other_lang, skipped_out_of_scope, resolved_detectors
   115→
   116→
   117→def upsert_findings(
   118→    existing: dict,
   119→    current_findings: list[dict],
   120→    ignore: list[str],
   121→    now: str,
   122→    *,
   123→    lang: str | None,
   124→) -> tuple[set[str], int, int, dict[str, int], int, set[str]]:
   125→    """Insert new findings and update existing ones.
   126→
   127→    Returns (current_ids, new_count, reopened_count, by_detector, ignored_count, changed_detectors).
   128→    """
   129→    current_ids: set[str] = set()
   130→    new_count = reopened_count = ignored_count = 0
   131→    by_detector: dict[str, int] = {}
   132→    changed_detectors: set[str] = set()
   133→
   134→    for finding in current_findings:
   135→        finding_id = finding["id"]
   136→        detector = finding.get("detector", "unknown")
   137→        current_ids.add(finding_id)
   138→        by_detector[detector] = by_detector.get(detector, 0) + 1
   139→        matched_ignore = matched_ignore_pattern(finding_id, finding["file"], ignore)
   140→        if matched_ignore:
   141→            ignored_count += 1
   142→
   143→        if lang:
   144→            finding["lang"] = lang
   145→
   146→        if finding_id not in existing:
   147→            existing[finding_id] = dict(finding)
   148→            if matched_ignore:
   149→                existing[finding_id]["suppressed"] = True
   150→                existing[finding_id]["suppressed_at"] = now
   151→                existing[finding_id]["suppression_pattern"] = matched_ignore
   152→                continue
   153→            new_count += 1
   154→            changed_detectors.add(detector)
   155→            continue
   156→
   157→        previous = existing[finding_id]
   158→        previous.update(
   159→            last_seen=now,
   160→            tier=finding["tier"],
   161→            confidence=finding["confidence"],
   162→            summary=finding["summary"],
   163→            detail=finding.get("detail", {}),
   164→        )
   165→        if "zone" in finding:
   166→            previous["zone"] = finding["zone"]
   167→        if lang and not previous.get("lang"):
   168→            previous["lang"] = lang
   169→
   170→        if matched_ignore:
   171→            previous["suppressed"] = True
   172→            previous["suppressed_at"] = now
   173→            previous["suppression_pattern"] = matched_ignore
   174→            continue
   175→
   176→        previous["suppressed"] = False
   177→        previous["suppressed_at"] = None
   178→        previous["suppression_pattern"] = None
   179→
   180→        if previous["status"] in ("fixed", "auto_resolved"):
   181→            # subjective_review findings are condition-based.  When just
   182→            # auto-resolved by an agent import, skip reopening to avoid a
   183→            # resolve-then-reopen loop on the same scan cycle.
   184→            if (
   185→                detector == "subjective_review"
   186→                and previous["status"] == "auto_resolved"
   187→                and (previous.get("resolution_attestation") or {}).get("kind") == "agent_import"
   188→            ):
   189→                continue
   190→            previous_status = previous["status"]
   191→            previous["reopen_count"] = previous.get("reopen_count", 0) + 1
   192→            previous.pop("resolution_attestation", None)
   193→            previous.update(
   194→                status="open",
   195→                resolved_at=None,
   196→                note=(
   197→                    f"Reopened (×{previous['reopen_count']}) "
   198→                    f"— reappeared in scan (was {previous_status})"
   199→                ),
   200→            )
   201→            reopened_count += 1
   202→            changed_detectors.add(detector)
   203→
   204→    return current_ids, new_count, reopened_count, by_detector, ignored_count, changed_detectors
   205→
   206→
   207→__all__ = [
   208→    "auto_resolve_disappeared",
   209→    "find_suspect_detectors",
   210→    "upsert_findings",
   211→]

1→"""Orphaned file detection: files with zero importers that aren't entry points."""
     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from collections.abc import Callable
     6→from dataclasses import dataclass
     7→from pathlib import Path
     8→
     9→from desloppify.base.file_paths import rel
    10→
    11→
    12→@dataclass
    13→class OrphanedDetectionOptions:
    14→    """Optional behavior flags for orphaned-file detection."""
    15→
    16→    extra_entry_patterns: list[str] | None = None
    17→    extra_barrel_names: set[str] | None = None
    18→    dynamic_import_finder: Callable[[Path, list[str]], set[str]] | None = None
    19→    alias_resolver: Callable[[str], str] | None = None
    20→
    21→
    22→def _is_dynamically_imported(
    23→    filepath: str,
    24→    dynamic_targets: set[str],
    25→    alias_resolver: Callable[[str], str] | None = None,
    26→) -> bool:
    27→    """Check if a file is referenced by any dynamic/side-effect import."""
    28→    r = rel(filepath)
    29→    stem = Path(filepath).stem
    30→    name_no_ext = str(Path(r).with_suffix(""))
    31→
    32→    for target in dynamic_targets:
    33→        resolved = alias_resolver(target) if alias_resolver else target
    34→        resolved = resolved.lstrip("./")
    35→        if resolved == name_no_ext or resolved == r:
    36→            return True
    37→        if name_no_ext.endswith("/" + resolved) or name_no_ext.endswith(resolved):
    38→            return True
    39→        if resolved.endswith("/" + stem) or resolved == stem:
    40→            return True
    41→        if resolved.endswith("/" + Path(filepath).name):
    42→            return True
    43→
    44→    return False
    45→
    46→
    47→def detect_orphaned_files(
    48→    path: Path,
    49→    graph: dict,
    50→    extensions: list[str],
    51→    options: OrphanedDetectionOptions | None = None,
    52→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    53→    """Find files with zero importers that aren't known entry points."""
    54→    resolved_options = options or OrphanedDetectionOptions()
    55→    all_entry_patterns = resolved_options.extra_entry_patterns or []
    56→    all_barrel_names = resolved_options.extra_barrel_names or set()
    57→    dynamic_import_finder = resolved_options.dynamic_import_finder
    58→    alias_resolver = resolved_options.alias_resolver
    59→
    60→    dynamic_targets = (
    61→        dynamic_import_finder(path, extensions) if dynamic_import_finder else set()
    62→    )
    63→
    64→    total_files = len(graph)
    65→    entries = []
    66→    for filepath, entry in graph.items():
    67→        if entry["importer_count"] > 0:
    68→            continue
    69→
    70→        r = rel(filepath)
    71→
    72→        if any(p in r for p in all_entry_patterns):
    73→            continue
    74→
    75→        basename = Path(filepath).name
    76→        if basename in all_barrel_names:
    77→            continue
    78→
    79→        if dynamic_targets and _is_dynamically_imported(
    80→            filepath, dynamic_targets, alias_resolver
    81→        ):
    82→            continue
    83→
    84→        try:
    85→            loc = len(Path(filepath).read_text().splitlines())
    86→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):
    87→            loc = 0
    88→
    89→        if loc < 10:
    90→            continue
    91→
    92→        entries.append(
    93→            {
    94→                "file": filepath,
    95→                "loc": loc,
    96→                "import_count": entry.get("import_count", 0),
    97→            }
    98→        )
    99→
   100→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["loc"]), total_files
   101→

     2→
     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→import os
     6→from collections import defaultdict
     7→
     8→from desloppify.base.registry import DETECTORS, DetectorMeta
     9→from desloppify.engine._plan.schema import Cluster, PlanModel, ensure_plan_defaults
    10→from desloppify.engine._plan.stale_dimensions import (
    11→    SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX,
    12→    _current_unscored_ids,
    13→)
    14→from desloppify.engine._state.schema import StateModel, utc_now
    15→
    16→AUTO_PREFIX = "auto/"
    17→_MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE = 2
    18→_STALE_KEY = "subjective::stale"
    19→_STALE_NAME = "auto/stale-review"
    20→_UNSCORED_KEY = "subjective::unscored"
    21→_UNSCORED_NAME = "auto/initial-review"
    22→_MIN_UNSCORED_CLUSTER_SIZE = 1
    23→
    24→
    25→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    26→# Grouping key computation
    27→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    28→
    29→def _extract_subtype(finding: dict) -> str | None:
    30→    """Extract the subtype/kind from a finding.
    31→
    32→    Checks detail.kind first, then falls back to parsing the finding ID
    33→    (format: ``detector::file::subtype`` or ``detector::file::symbol::subtype``).
    34→    """
    35→    detail = finding.get("detail") or {}
    36→    kind = detail.get("kind")
    37→    if kind:
    38→        return kind
    39→
    40→    # Parse from finding ID — third segment is often the subtype
    41→    fid = finding.get("id", "")
    42→    parts = fid.split("::")
    43→    if len(parts) >= 3:
    44→        # For IDs like smells::file.py::silent_except, the subtype is parts[2]
    45→        # For IDs like dict_keys::file.py::key::phantom_read, subtype is last part
    46→        candidate = parts[-1]
    47→        # Skip if it looks like a file path or symbol name (contains / or .)
    48→        if "/" not in candidate and "." not in candidate:
    49→            return candidate
    50→    return None
    51→
    52→
    53→def _grouping_key(finding: dict, meta: DetectorMeta | None) -> str | None:
    54→    """Compute a deterministic grouping key for a finding.
    55→
    56→    Returns None if the finding should not be auto-clustered.
    57→    """
    58→    detector = finding.get("detector", "")
    59→
    60→    if meta is None:
    61→        # Unknown detector — group by detector name
    62→        return f"detector::{detector}"
    63→
    64→    # Review findings → group by dimension
    65→    if detector in ("review", "subjective_review"):
    66→        detail = finding.get("detail") or {}
    67→        dimension = detail.get("dimension", "")
    68→        if dimension:
    69→            return f"review::{dimension}"
    70→        return f"detector::{detector}"
    71→
    72→    # Per-file detectors (structural, responsibility_cohesion)
    73→    if meta.needs_judgment and detector in (
    74→        "structural", "responsibility_cohesion",
    75→    ):
    76→        file = finding.get("file", "")
    77→        if file:
    78→            basename = os.path.basename(file)
    79→            return f"file::{detector}::{basename}"
    80→
    81→    # Needs-judgment detectors — group by subtype when available
    82→    if meta.needs_judgment:
    83→        subtype = _extract_subtype(finding)
    84→        if subtype:
    85→            return f"typed::{detector}::{subtype}"
    86→
    87→    # Pure auto-fix (no judgment needed) → all findings by detector
    88→    if meta.action_type == "auto_fix" and not meta.needs_judgment:
    89→        return f"auto::{detector}"
    90→
    91→    # Everything else → by detector
    92→    return f"detector::{detector}"
    93→
    94→
    95→def _cluster_name_from_key(key: str) -> str:
    96→    """Convert a grouping key to a cluster name with auto/ prefix."""
    97→    # auto::unused → auto/unused
    98→    # typed::dict_keys::phantom_read → auto/dict_keys-phantom_read
    99→    # file::structural::big_file.py → auto/structural-big_file.py
   100→    # review::abstraction_fitness → auto/review-abstraction_fitness
   101→    # detector::security → auto/security
   102→    parts = key.split("::")
   103→    if len(parts) == 2:
   104→        prefix_type = parts[0]
   105→        # For review keys, keep the prefix for clarity
   106→        if prefix_type == "review":
   107→            return f"{AUTO_PREFIX}review-{parts[1]}"
   108→        return f"{AUTO_PREFIX}{parts[1]}"
   109→    if len(parts) == 3:
   110→        return f"{AUTO_PREFIX}{parts[1]}-{parts[2]}"
   111→    return f"{AUTO_PREFIX}{key.replace('::', '-')}"
   112→
   113→
   114→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   115→# Description and action generation
   116→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   117→
   118→def _generate_description(
   119→    cluster_name: str,
   120→    members: list[dict],
   121→    meta: DetectorMeta | None,
   122→    subtype: str | None,
   123→) -> str:
   124→    """Generate a human-readable cluster description."""
   125→    count = len(members)
   126→    detector = members[0].get("detector", "") if members else ""
   127→
   128→    if detector in ("review", "subjective_review"):
   129→        detail = (members[0].get("detail") or {}) if members else {}
   130→        dimension = detail.get("dimension", detector)
   131→        return f"Address {count} {dimension} review findings"
   132→
   133→    if detector == "structural":
   134→        files = {os.path.basename(m.get("file", "")) for m in members}
   135→        if len(files) == 1:
   136→            return f"Decompose {next(iter(files))}"
   137→        return f"Decompose {count} large files"
   138→
   139→    display = meta.display if meta else detector
   140→    if subtype:
   141→        label = subtype.replace("_", " ")
   142→        return f"Fix {count} {label} issues"
   143→
   144→    if meta and meta.action_type == "auto_fix" and not meta.needs_judgment:
   145→        return f"Remove {count} {display} findings"
   146→
   147→    return f"Fix {count} {display} issues"
   148→
   149→
   150→def _subtype_has_fixer(meta: DetectorMeta, subtype: str | None) -> str | None:
   151→    """Check if a subtype maps to a specific fixer."""
   152→    if not meta.fixers or not subtype:
   153→        return None
   154→    # Convention: fixer name is subtype with _ replaced by -
   155→    fixer_name = subtype.replace("_", "-")
   156→    if fixer_name in meta.fixers:
   157→        return fixer_name
   158→    # Also check if subtype is a substring (e.g. "unused" matches "unused-imports")
   159→    for fixer in meta.fixers:
   160→        if subtype in fixer:
   161→            return fixer
   162→    return None
   163→
   164→
   165→def _strip_guidance_examples(guidance: str) -> str:
   166→    """Strip subtype-specific examples from guidance text.
   167→
   168→    Many guidance strings have format "verb — specific examples".
   169→    Strip after the dash to get the core action:
   170→      "fix code smells — dead useEffect, empty if chains" → "fix code smells"
   171→    """
   172→    if " — " in guidance:
   173→        return guidance.split(" — ", 1)[0].strip()
   174→    return guidance
   175→
   176→
   177→_ACTION_TYPE_TEMPLATES: dict[str, str] = {
   178→    "reorganize": "reorganize with desloppify move",
   179→    "refactor": "review and refactor each finding",
   180→    "manual_fix": "review and fix each finding",
   181→}
   182→
   183→
   184→def _generate_action(
   185→    meta: DetectorMeta | None,
   186→    subtype: str | None,
   187→) -> str:
   188→    """Generate an action string from detector metadata.
   189→
   190→    Always returns a non-empty string — every cluster gets an action.
   191→    """
   192→    if meta is None:
   193→        return "review and fix each finding"
   194→
   195→    # For detectors with subtypes, only suggest a fixer if the subtype matches
   196→    if subtype and meta.fixers:
   197→        matched_fixer = _subtype_has_fixer(meta, subtype)
   198→        if matched_fixer:
   199→            return f"desloppify fix {matched_fixer} --dry-run"
   200→    elif meta.action_type == "auto_fix" and meta.fixers and not meta.needs_judgment:
   201→        # Pure auto-fix detector, no subtypes
   202→        return f"desloppify fix {meta.fixers[0]} --dry-run"
   203→
   204→    if meta.tool == "move":
   205→        return "desloppify move"
   206→
   207→    # Guidance available — use it (strip examples for subtyped detectors)
   208→    if meta.guidance:
   209→        if subtype:
   210→            return _strip_guidance_examples(meta.guidance)
   211→        return meta.guidance
   212→
   213→    # Final fallback: action_type template
   214→    return _ACTION_TYPE_TEMPLATES.get(
   215→        meta.action_type, "review and fix each finding"
   216→    )
   217→
   218→
   219→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   220→# Main algorithm
   221→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   222→
   223→def auto_cluster_findings(plan: PlanModel, state: StateModel) -> int:
   224→    """Regenerate auto-clusters from current open findings.
   225→
   226→    Returns count of changes made (clusters created, updated, or deleted).
   227→    """
   228→    ensure_plan_defaults(plan)
   229→    changes = 0
   230→
   231→    findings = state.get("findings", {})
   232→    clusters = plan.get("clusters", {})
   233→
   234→    # Set of finding IDs in manual (non-auto) clusters
   235→    manual_member_ids: set[str] = set()
   236→    for cluster in clusters.values():
   237→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
   238→            manual_member_ids.update(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   239→
   240→    # Collect open, non-suppressed findings and group by key
   241→    groups: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
   242→    finding_data: dict[str, dict] = {}
   243→    for fid, finding in findings.items():
   244→        if finding.get("status") != "open":
   245→            continue
   246→        if finding.get("suppressed"):
   247→            continue
   248→        if fid in manual_member_ids:
   249→            continue
   250→
   251→        detector = finding.get("detector", "")
   252→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   253→        key = _grouping_key(finding, meta)
   254→        if key is None:
   255→            continue
   256→
   257→        groups[key].append(fid)
   258→        finding_data[fid] = finding
   259→
   260→    # Drop singleton groups
   261→    groups = {k: v for k, v in groups.items() if len(v) >= _MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE}
   262→
   263→    # Map existing auto-clusters by cluster_key
   264→    existing_by_key: dict[str, str] = {}  # cluster_key → cluster_name
   265→    for name, cluster in list(clusters.items()):
   266→        if cluster.get("auto"):
   267→            ck = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
   268→            if ck:
   269→                existing_by_key[ck] = name
   270→
   271→    now = utc_now()
   272→    active_auto_keys: set[str] = set()
   273→
   274→    for key, member_ids in groups.items():
   275→        active_auto_keys.add(key)
   276→        cluster_name = _cluster_name_from_key(key)
   277→
   278→        # Representative finding for metadata
   279→        rep = finding_data.get(member_ids[0], {})
   280→        detector = rep.get("detector", "")
   281→        meta = DETECTORS.get(detector)
   282→        members = [finding_data[fid] for fid in member_ids if fid in finding_data]
   283→
   284→        # Extract subtype from grouping key (typed::detector::subtype)
   285→        key_parts = key.split("::")
   286→        subtype = key_parts[2] if len(key_parts) >= 3 else None
   287→
   288→        description = _generate_description(cluster_name, members, meta, subtype)
   289→        action = _generate_action(meta, subtype)
   290→
   291→        existing_name = existing_by_key.get(key)
   292→        if existing_name and existing_name in clusters:
   293→            cluster = clusters[existing_name]
   294→            if cluster.get("user_modified"):
   295→                # Merge new findings in, don't remove user's edits
   296→                existing_ids = set(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   297→                new_ids = [fid for fid in member_ids if fid not in existing_ids]
   298→                if new_ids:
   299→                    cluster["finding_ids"].extend(new_ids)
   300→                    cluster["updated_at"] = now
   301→                    changes += 1
   302→            else:
   303→                # Replace membership wholesale
   304→                old_ids = set(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   305→                new_ids = set(member_ids)
   306→                if old_ids != new_ids or cluster.get("description") != description or cluster.get("action") != action:
   307→                    cluster["finding_ids"] = list(member_ids)
   308→                    cluster["description"] = description
   309→                    cluster["action"] = action
   310→                    cluster["updated_at"] = now
   311→                    changes += 1
   312→        else:
   313→            # Handle name collision (existing auto-cluster with different key)
   314→            # If cluster_name already exists with a different key, skip
   315→            if cluster_name in clusters and clusters[cluster_name].get("cluster_key") != key:
   316→                # Append a disambiguator
   317→                cluster_name = f"{cluster_name}-{len(member_ids)}"
   318→
   319→            new_cluster: Cluster = {
   320→                "name": cluster_name,
   321→                "description": description,
   322→                "finding_ids": list(member_ids),
   323→                "created_at": now,
   324→                "updated_at": now,
   325→                "auto": True,
   326→                "cluster_key": key,
   327→                "action": action,
   328→                "user_modified": False,
   329→            }
   330→            clusters[cluster_name] = new_cluster
   331→            existing_by_key[key] = cluster_name
   332→            changes += 1
   333→
   334→        # Update overrides to track cluster membership
   335→        overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
   336→        current_name = existing_by_key.get(key, cluster_name)
   337→        for fid in member_ids:
   338→            if fid not in overrides:
   339→                overrides[fid] = {"finding_id": fid, "created_at": now}
   340→            overrides[fid]["cluster"] = current_name
   341→            overrides[fid]["updated_at"] = now
   342→
   343→    # --- Subjective dimension clusters (unscored + stale) -------------------
   344→    all_subjective_ids = sorted(
   345→        fid for fid in plan.get("queue_order", [])
   346→        if fid.startswith(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX)
   347→    )
   348→    unscored_state_ids = _current_unscored_ids(state)
   349→    unscored_queue_ids = sorted(
   350→        fid for fid in all_subjective_ids if fid in unscored_state_ids
   351→    )
   352→    stale_queue_ids = sorted(
   353→        fid for fid in all_subjective_ids if fid not in unscored_state_ids
   354→    )
   355→
   356→    # -- Initial review cluster (unscored, min size 1) ---------------------
   357→    if len(unscored_queue_ids) >= _MIN_UNSCORED_CLUSTER_SIZE:
   358→        active_auto_keys.add(_UNSCORED_KEY)
   359→        cli_keys = [fid.removeprefix(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) for fid in unscored_queue_ids]
   360→        description = f"Initial review of {len(unscored_queue_ids)} unscored subjective dimensions"
   361→        action = f"desloppify review --prepare --dimensions {','.join(cli_keys)}"
   362→
   363→        existing_name = existing_by_key.get(_UNSCORED_KEY)
   364→        if existing_name and existing_name in clusters:
   365→            cluster = clusters[existing_name]
   366→            old_ids = set(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   367→            new_ids = set(unscored_queue_ids)
   368→            if old_ids != new_ids or cluster.get("description") != description or cluster.get("action") != action:
   369→                cluster["finding_ids"] = unscored_queue_ids
   370→                cluster["description"] = description
   371→                cluster["action"] = action
   372→                cluster["updated_at"] = now
   373→                changes += 1
   374→        else:
   375→            clusters[_UNSCORED_NAME] = {
   376→                "name": _UNSCORED_NAME,
   377→                "description": description,
   378→                "finding_ids": unscored_queue_ids,
   379→                "created_at": now,
   380→                "updated_at": now,
   381→                "auto": True,
   382→                "cluster_key": _UNSCORED_KEY,
   383→                "action": action,
   384→                "user_modified": False,
   385→            }
   386→            existing_by_key[_UNSCORED_KEY] = _UNSCORED_NAME
   387→            changes += 1
   388→
   389→        overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
   390→        current_name = existing_by_key.get(_UNSCORED_KEY, _UNSCORED_NAME)
   391→        for fid in unscored_queue_ids:
   392→            if fid not in overrides:
   393→                overrides[fid] = {"finding_id": fid, "created_at": now}
   394→            overrides[fid]["cluster"] = current_name
   395→            overrides[fid]["updated_at"] = now
   396→
   397→    # -- Stale review cluster (previously scored, min size 2) --------------
   398→    if len(stale_queue_ids) >= _MIN_CLUSTER_SIZE:
   399→        active_auto_keys.add(_STALE_KEY)
   400→        cli_keys = [fid.removeprefix(SUBJECTIVE_PREFIX) for fid in stale_queue_ids]
   401→        description = f"Re-review {len(stale_queue_ids)} stale subjective dimensions"
   402→        action = f"desloppify review --prepare --dimensions {','.join(cli_keys)}"
   403→
   404→        existing_name = existing_by_key.get(_STALE_KEY)
   405→        if existing_name and existing_name in clusters:
   406→            cluster = clusters[existing_name]
   407→            old_ids = set(cluster.get("finding_ids", []))
   408→            new_ids = set(stale_queue_ids)
   409→            if old_ids != new_ids or cluster.get("description") != description or cluster.get("action") != action:
   410→                cluster["finding_ids"] = stale_queue_ids
   411→                cluster["description"] = description
   412→                cluster["action"] = action
   413→                cluster["updated_at"] = now
   414→                changes += 1
   415→        else:
   416→            clusters[_STALE_NAME] = {
   417→                "name": _STALE_NAME,
   418→                "description": description,
   419→                "finding_ids": stale_queue_ids,
   420→                "created_at": now,
   421→                "updated_at": now,
   422→                "auto": True,
   423→                "cluster_key": _STALE_KEY,
   424→                "action": action,
   425→                "user_modified": False,
   426→            }
   427→            existing_by_key[_STALE_KEY] = _STALE_NAME
   428→            changes += 1
   429→
   430→        overrides = plan.get("overrides", {})
   431→        current_name = existing_by_key.get(_STALE_KEY, _STALE_NAME)
   432→        for fid in stale_queue_ids:
   433→            if fid not in overrides:
   434→                overrides[fid] = {"finding_id": fid, "created_at": now}
   435→            overrides[fid]["cluster"] = current_name
   436→            overrides[fid]["updated_at"] = now
   437→
   438→    # Delete stale auto-clusters (no matching group, not user_modified)
   439→    for name in list(clusters.keys()):
   440→        cluster = clusters[name]
   441→        if not cluster.get("auto"):
   442→            continue
   443→        ck = cluster.get("cluster_key", "")
   444→        if ck in active_auto_keys:
   445→            continue
   446→        if cluster.get("user_modified"):
   447→            # Keep user-modified clusters but prune dead member IDs
   448→            alive = [fid for fid in cluster.get("finding_ids", [])
   449→                     if fid in findings and findings[fid].get("status") == "open"]
   450→            if alive:
   451→                if len(alive) != len(cluster.get("finding_ids", [])):
   452→                    cluster["finding_ids"] = alive
   453→                    cluster["updated_at"] = now
   454→                    changes += 1
   455→                continue
   456→            # All members gone — delete even if user_modified
   457→        # Delete stale cluster
   458→        del clusters[name]
   459→        # Clear cluster refs from overrides
   460→        for fid in cluster.get("finding_ids", []):
   461→            override = plan.get("overrides", {}).get(fid)
   462→            if override and override.get("cluster") == name:
   463→                override["cluster"] = None
   464→                override["updated_at"] = now
   465→        if plan.get("active_cluster") == name:
   466→            plan["active_cluster"] = None
   467→        changes += 1
   468→
   469→    plan["updated"] = now
   470→    return changes
   471→
   472→
   473→__all__ = [
   474→    "AUTO_PREFIX",
   475→    "auto_cluster_findings",
   476→]
   477→

   119→        0,
   120→        CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(item.get("confidence", "low"), 9),
   121→        -review_weight,
   122→        -int(detail.get("count", 0) or 0),
   123→        item.get("id", ""),
   124→    )
   125→
   126→
   127→def item_explain(item: dict) -> dict:
   128→    effective_tier = int(item.get("effective_tier", item.get("tier", 3)))
   129→
   130→    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":
   131→        return {
   132→            "kind": "subjective_dimension",
   133→            "effective_tier": effective_tier,
   134→            "subjective_score": subjective_score_value(item),
   135→            "policy": (
   136→                "Subjective dimensions are always queued as T4 and do not outrank "
   137→                "mechanical T1/T2/T3 items."
   138→            ),
   139→            "ranking_factors": ["tier asc", "subjective_score asc", "id asc"],
   140→        }
   141→
   142→    detail = detail_dict(item)
   143→    confidence = item.get("confidence", "low")
   144→    is_subjective = bool(item.get("is_subjective"))
   145→    is_review = bool(item.get("is_review"))
   146→    ranking_factors: list[str]
   147→    if is_subjective:
   148→        ranking_factors = ["tier fixed to T4", "subjective_score asc", "id asc"]
   149→    elif is_review:
   150→        ranking_factors = [
   151→            "tier asc",
   152→            "confidence asc",
   153→            "review_weight desc",
   154→            "count desc",
   155→            "id asc",
   156→        ]
   157→    else:
   158→        ranking_factors = ["tier asc", "confidence asc", "count desc", "id asc"]
   159→    explain = {
   160→        "kind": "finding",
   161→        "effective_tier": effective_tier,
   162→        "confidence": confidence,
   163→        "confidence_rank": CONFIDENCE_ORDER.get(confidence, 9),
   164→        "count": int(detail.get("count", 0) or 0),
   165→        "id": item.get("id", ""),
   166→        "ranking_factors": ranking_factors,
   167→    }
   168→    if is_review:
   169→        explain["review_weight"] = float(item.get("review_weight", 0.0) or 0.0)
   170→    if is_subjective:
   171→        explain["policy"] = (
   172→            "Subjective findings are forced to T4 and do not outrank "
   173→            "mechanical T1/T2/T3 items."
   174→        )
   175→        explain["subjective_score"] = subjective_score_value(item)
   176→    return explain
   177→
   178→
   179→def tier_counts(items: list[dict]) -> dict[int, int]:
   180→    counts = {1: 0, 2: 0, 3: 0, 4: 0}
   181→    for item in items:
   182→        if item.get("kind") == "cluster":
   183→            # Count each member at its own tier
   184→            for member in item.get("members", []):
   185→                tier = int(member.get("effective_tier", member.get("tier", 3)))
   186→                counts[tier] = counts.get(tier, 0) + 1
   187→            continue
   188→        tier = int(item.get("effective_tier", item.get("tier", 3)))
   189→        counts[tier] = counts.get(tier, 0) + 1
   190→    return counts
   191→
   192→
   193→def choose_fallback_tier(requested_tier: int, counts: dict[int, int]) -> int | None:
   194→    available = [tier for tier, count in counts.items() if count > 0]
   195→    if not available:
   196→        return None
   197→    return min(available, key=lambda tier: (abs(tier - requested_tier), tier))
   198→
   199→
   200→def group_queue_items(items: list[dict], group: str) -> dict[str, list[dict]]:
   201→    """Group queue items for alternate output modes."""
   202→    grouped: dict[str, list[dict]] = {}
   203→    for item in items:
   204→        if group == "file":
   205→            key = item.get("file", "")
   206→        elif group == "detector":
   207→            key = item.get("detector", "")
   208→        elif group == "tier":
   209→            key = f"T{int(item.get('effective_tier', item.get('tier', 3)))}"
   210→        elif group == "cluster":
   211→            plan_cluster = item.get("plan_cluster")
   212→            key = plan_cluster["name"] if isinstance(plan_cluster, dict) else "(unclustered)"
   213→        else:
   214→            key = "items"
   215→        grouped.setdefault(key, []).append(item)
   216→    return grouped
   217→
   218→
   219→__all__ = [
   220→    "build_finding_items",
   221→    "choose_fallback_tier",
   222→    "item_explain",
   223→    "item_sort_key",
   224→    "tier_counts",
   225→    "subjective_score_value",
   226→    "group_queue_items",
   227→]

   247→def coerce_target_score(value: object, *, fallback: float = 95.0) -> float:
   248→    """Normalize target score-like values to a safe [0, 100] float."""
   249→    if is_numeric(fallback):
   250→        fallback_value = float(fallback)
   251→    else:
   252→        fallback_value = 95.0
   253→
   254→    if is_numeric(value):
   255→        parsed = float(value)
   256→    elif isinstance(value, str):
   257→        text = value.strip()
   258→        if not text:
   259→            parsed = fallback_value
   260→        else:
   261→            try:
   262→                parsed = float(text)
   263→            except ValueError:
   264→                parsed = fallback_value
   265→    else:
   266→        parsed = fallback_value
   267→    return max(0.0, min(100.0, parsed))

   302→def _migrate_from_state_files(config_path: Path) -> dict:
   303→    """Migrate config keys from state-*.json files into config.json.
   304→
   305→    Reads state["config"] from all state files, merges them (union for
   306→    lists, merge for dicts), writes config.json, and strips "config" from
   307→    the state files.
   308→    """
   309→    config: dict = {}
   310→    state_dir = config_path.parent
   311→    if not state_dir.exists():
   312→        return config
   313→
   314→    state_files = list(state_dir.glob("state-*.json")) + list(
   315→        state_dir.glob("state.json")
   316→    )
   317→    migrated_any = False
   318→    for sf in state_files:
   319→        try:
   320→            state_data = json.loads(sf.read_text())
   321→        except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError, OSError) as exc:
   322→            logger.debug("Skipping unreadable state file %s: %s", sf, exc)
   323→            continue

   325→        old_config = state_data.get("config")
   326→        if not old_config or not isinstance(old_config, dict):
   327→            continue
   328→
   329→        # Merge: union for lists, merge for dicts, first-wins for scalars
   330→        for k, v in old_config.items():
   331→            if k not in CONFIG_SCHEMA:
   332→                continue
   333→            _merge_config_value(config, k, v)
   334→
   335→        # Strip "config" from state file
   336→        if "config" in state_data:
   337→            del state_data["config"]
   338→            try:
   339→                safe_write_text(sf, json.dumps(state_data, indent=2) + "\n")
   340→            except OSError as exc:
   341→                log_best_effort_failure(
   342→                    logger,
   343→                    f"rewrite state file {sf} after config migration",
   344→                    exc,
   345→                )
   346→
   347→        migrated_any = True
   348→
   349→    if migrated_any and config:
   350→        try:
   351→            save_config(config, config_path)
   352→        except OSError as exc:
   353→            log_best_effort_failure(
   354→                logger, f"save migrated config to {config_path}", exc
   355→            )
   356→
   357→    return config
   358→
```

   339→    global JUDGMENT_DETECTORS

   369→def dimension_action_type(dim_name: str) -> str:
   370→    """Return a compact action type label for a dimension based on its detectors."""
   371→    best = "manual"
   372→    best_pri = 99
   373→    for d in DETECTORS.values():
   374→        if d.dimension == dim_name:
   375→            pri = _ACTION_PRIORITY.get(d.action_type, 99)
   376→            if pri < best_pri:
   377→                best_pri = pri
   378→                best = d.action_type
   379→    return _ACTION_LABELS.get(best, "manual")

   382→def detector_tools() -> dict[str, dict]:
   383→    """Build detector tool metadata keyed by detector name."""
   384→    result = {}

   386→        entry: dict = {

   392→        if d.guidance:
   393→            entry["guidance"] = d.guidance
   394→        result[name] = entry

1→"""Complexity signal detection: configurable per-language complexity signals."""
     2→
     3→import inspect
     4→import logging
     5→import re
     6→from pathlib import Path
     7→
     8→from desloppify.base.fallbacks import log_best_effort_failure
     9→from desloppify.base.file_paths import resolve_scan_file
    10→
    11→logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
    12→
    13→
    14→def detect_complexity(
    15→    path: Path, signals, file_finder, threshold: int = 15, min_loc: int = 50
    16→) -> tuple[list[dict], int]:
    17→    """Detect files with complexity signals.
    18→
    19→    Args:
    20→        path: Directory to scan.
    21→        signals: list of ComplexitySignal objects. Required.
    22→        file_finder: callable(path) -> list[str]. Required.
    23→        threshold: minimum score to flag a file.
    24→        min_loc: minimum LOC to consider.
    25→
    26→    Returns:
    27→        (entries, total_files_checked)
    28→    """
    29→    files = file_finder(path)
    30→    entries = []
    31→    for filepath in files:
    32→        try:
    33→            p = resolve_scan_file(filepath, scan_root=path)
    34→            content = p.read_text()
    35→            lines = content.splitlines()
    36→            loc = len(lines)
    37→            if loc < min_loc:
    38→                continue
    39→
    40→            file_signals = []
    41→            score = 0
    42→
    43→            for sig in signals:
    44→                try:
    45→                    if sig.compute:
    46→                        # Pass filepath to compute fns that accept it (tree-sitter signals).
    47→                        accepts_filepath = "_filepath" in inspect.signature(
    48→                            sig.compute
    49→                        ).parameters
    50→                        if accepts_filepath:
    51→                            result = sig.compute(content, lines, _filepath=filepath)
    52→                        else:
    53→                            result = sig.compute(content, lines)
    54→                        if result:
    55→                            count, label = result
    56→                            file_signals.append(label)
    57→                            excess = (
    58→                                max(0, count - sig.threshold) if sig.threshold else count
    59→                            )
    60→                            score += excess * sig.weight
    61→                    elif sig.pattern:
    62→                        count = len(re.findall(sig.pattern, content, re.MULTILINE))
    63→                        if count > sig.threshold:
    64→                            file_signals.append(f"{count} {sig.name}")
    65→                            score += (count - sig.threshold) * sig.weight
    66→                except (TypeError, ValueError, KeyError, AttributeError, re.error) as exc:
    67→                    log_best_effort_failure(
    68→                        logger,
    69→                        f"compute complexity signal '{sig.name}' for {filepath}",
    70→                        exc,
    71→                    )
    72→                    continue
    73→
    74→            if file_signals and score >= threshold:
    75→                entries.append(
    76→                    {
    77→                        "file": filepath,
    78→                        "loc": loc,
    79→                        "score": score,
    80→                        "signals": file_signals,
    81→                    }
    82→                )
    83→        except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError) as exc:
    84→            log_best_effort_failure(
    85→                logger,
    86→                f"read complexity detector candidate {filepath}",
    87→                exc,
    88→            )
    89→            continue
    90→    return sorted(entries, key=lambda e: -e["score"]), len(files)
    91→

     3→from __future__ import annotations
     4→
     5→from desloppify.engine._work_queue.helpers import (
     6→    detail_dict,
     7→    is_review_finding,
     8→    is_subjective_finding,
     9→    primary_command_for_finding,
    10→    review_finding_weight,
    11→    scope_matches,
    12→    slugify,
    13→    status_matches,
    14→    subjective_strict_scores,
    15→    supported_fixers_for_item,
    16→)
    17→from desloppify.engine.planning.common import CONFIDENCE_ORDER
    18→from desloppify.state import path_scoped_findings
    19→
    20→
    21→def subjective_score_value(item: dict) -> float:
    22→    if item.get("kind") == "subjective_dimension":
    23→        detail = detail_dict(item)
    24→        return float(detail.get("strict_score", item.get("subjective_score", 100.0)))
    25→    return float(item.get("subjective_score", 100.0))
    26→
    27→
    28→def build_finding_items(
    29→    state: dict,
    30→    *,
    31→    scan_path: str | None,
    32→    status_filter: str,
    33→    scope: str | None,
    34→    chronic: bool,
    35→) -> list[dict]:
    36→    scoped = path_scoped_findings(state.get("findings", {}), scan_path)
    37→    subjective_scores = subjective_strict_scores(state)
    38→    out: list[dict] = []
    39→
    40→    for finding_id, finding in scoped.items():
    41→        if finding.get("suppressed"):
    42→            continue
    43→        if not status_matches(finding.get("status", "open"), status_filter):
    44→            continue
    45→        if chronic and not (
    46→            finding.get("status") == "open" and finding.get("reopen_count", 0) >= 2
    47→        ):
    48→            continue
    49→
    50→        item = dict(finding)
    51→        item["id"] = finding_id
    52→        item["kind"] = "finding"
    53→        item["is_review"] = is_review_finding(item)
    54→        item["is_subjective"] = is_subjective_finding(item)
    55→        item["effective_tier"] = (
    56→            4 if item["is_subjective"] else int(finding.get("tier", 3))
    57→        )
    58→        item["review_weight"] = (
    59→            review_finding_weight(item) if item["is_review"] else None
    60→        )
    61→        subjective_score = None
    62→        if item["is_subjective"]:
    63→            detail = detail_dict(finding)
    64→            dim_name = detail.get("dimension_name", "")
    65→            dim_key = detail.get("dimension", "") or slugify(dim_name)
    66→            subjective_score = subjective_scores.get(
    67→                dim_key, subjective_scores.get(dim_name.lower(), 100.0)
    68→            )
    69→        item["subjective_score"] = subjective_score
    70→        supported_fixers = supported_fixers_for_item(state, item)
    71→        item["primary_command"] = primary_command_for_finding(
    72→            item,
    73→            supported_fixers=supported_fixers,
    74→        )
    75→
    76→        if not scope_matches(item, scope):
    77→            continue
    78→        out.append(item)
    79→
    80→    return out
